localAgencies.notes: ADEQ states EPA Region 9 issues air permits on tribal lands, excluding the Navajo Nation and Gila River Indian Community.

overview: ADEQ issues Class I (major/Title V) and Class II individual permits, general permits, and registrations everywhere except Maricopa, Pima, and Pinal counties, which run their own permitting, inspection, and enforcement programs. EPA Region 9 permits on most tribal lands.

permitTypes.name: Air Quality Registration
permitTypes.description: Registration application for qualifying smaller sources.

permitTypes.name: General Permits
permitTypes.description: Pre-approved permits for classes of similar sources; an Authorization to Operate is issued for each major piece of equipment. ADEQ general permits include air curtain incinerators, concrete batch plants, crushing and screening, hospitals, hot mix asphalt, soil vapor extraction, and dust action.

permitTypes.name: Class II Individual Permit
permitTypes.description: For sources that do not qualify for Class I but meet A.A.C. R18-2-302(B)(2), including sources with potential to emit significant quantities and sources subject to CAA sections 111 or 112 (with listed exceptions). Valid five years.

permitTypes.name: Class I Individual Permit (Title V)
permitTypes.description: Major sources; Arizona's Title V program is EPA-approved. Valid five years.
permitTypes.citation: A.A.C. R18-2-302(B)(1); major source definition R18-2-101
permitTypes.thresholds: Per ADEQ: 100 tons/year or more of any criteria pollutant, 10 tons/year or more of any single HAP, or 25 tons/year or more of combined HAPs.

permitTypes.name: PSD permit
permitTypes.description: Required before construction of new major sources and major modifications in attainment areas.

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment NSR permit
permitTypes.description: Required before construction of new major sources and major modifications in nonattainment areas.

oilAndGas.summary: ADEQ's air permitting pages reviewed list no oil-and-gas-specific air permit or rule. Oil and gas sources use Class I/II individual permits; federal NSPS and NESHAP apply.
